findings.fix: Collect the house number and street together in one address-line field.
findings.violation: The house number has its own field separate from the street, and it is required, so an address with no number cannot be entered.

findings.fix: Replace it with the standard token for this field, for example email.
findings.violation: The autocomplete value e-mail is not a valid autofill detail in the HTML standard, so autofill is broken for this field.

findings.evidence: <select id="hear-select" required=""> with options Search engine, Social media, Friend or colleague, Advertisement, Other, inside a form headed 'Create your account' whose only action is a button labelled Submit.
findings.fix: Remove the field from account creation, or make it optional and ask it after the account exists.
findings.location: #hear-select, <select> field, label 'How did you hear about us?', line 84
findings.violation: The task this form performs, named by its heading and its submit action, is creating an account, which has no use for how the person heard about the service; the field is required, so the task cannot proceed without an answer it cannot use.

findings.evidence: <button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button>, sitting between the field at #row-contacttime (line 77-80) and the field at #row-hear (line 82-91), with the primary submit button only at line 92.
findings.fix: Move 'View details' out of the field sequence, for example beside or below the primary submit, or remove it, so the only controls a person meets while filling fields are the fields themselves.
findings.violation: A secondary action with explicit padding and font-size, giving it visible weight, sits inside the column of fields between two required fields rather than beside or after the primary action, where FORMS-ACTION-HIERARCHY expects every action to sit in line with where the fields end.

findings.fix: Label the button with the action it performs, such as Create account or Send message.
findings.violation: The form's primary button is labelled Submit, a generic word that says nothing about what pressing it does.
On this name field, autocorrection and spellchecking stay on, so a phone keyboard can change a value it does not know.

findings.fix: Remove the confirmation field and offer a control that shows the password as typed.
findings.violation: The form asks for the new password a second time to confirm it, doubling the typing for every person.

findings.evidence: <input id="name-input" name="full_name" type="text" autocomplete="name" required=""> at line 12, labelled 'Full name', and <input id="legalname-input" name="legal_name" type="text" autocomplete="name" required=""> at line 71, labelled 'Your name', both carrying the same autocomplete token and both required.
findings.fix: Remove the second name field, or, if the two genuinely differ (for example a legal name for billing versus a display name), say so in both labels.
findings.violation: The form asks for the person's name a second time under a different label, with nothing in either label or the surrounding markup stating what distinguishes the two, so the person must re-enter data the form already asked for or guess why it is asking again.
